correctness.rationale: For nonzero x and y, a vanishing product forces c=x^(1-q^r)y^(1-q^s), of norm one. For x nonzero, writing y=xt cancels the xy term and leaves t^(q^r)=t^(q^s); the solutions, including t=0, form the fixed field F_(q^g). Zero commutes with all elements. The H-lines partition K minus zero; any commuting set with a nonzero element lies in one line. This gives the maximal additive subspaces, the disjoint cliques, and the count by placing every tuple except the all-zero tuple in a unique line. For n=6 both differences have gcd 2. Albert's theorem applies: both one-sided nuclei have order q for (1,5), and both have order q² for (2,4), after unital normalization; this is the intended comparison at RESULT.md line 21, as made explicit at line 43. As an independent check, write the left multiplication spread as L_x=M_x-M_(c x^(q^r))F^s, with F the q-Frobenius and M scalar multiplication. If A=sum a_j F^j belongs to its left composition idealizer, then for j outside {0,s} the coefficient of F^j in A L_x vanishes identically in x. It is a_j x^(q^j)-a_(j-s)c^(q^(j-s))x^(q^(r+j-s)), with indices modulo 6. The two powers are independent over K, since r!=s. Thus a_i can survive only when i and i+s both belong to {0,s}; as 2s is nonzero modulo 6 for these examples, A=M_a. Matching F^s then gives a^(q^r)=a. The opposite spread yields the right nucleus by the same argument. Under isotopy the left composition idealizer changes by conjugation; for a unital product, applying an idealizer element to L_1 shows it is L_a, and the idealizer identity is exactly left-nucleus associativity. The idealizer calculation is over F_q; the cited nucleus theorem establishes the obstruction to isotopy without requiring an F_q-linear isotopy. value.rationale: This is a structural counterexample about a natural observation on a classical family. Even the full labeled relation on the common field cannot recover isotopy, a strictly stronger obstruction than equality of tuple counts or of an abstract graph. The proof isolates why: relative Frobenius controls commutation, while the individual twists control the distinguishing nucleus orders. The arity formula packages the complete profile once that mechanism is known.
